text:
chris: quick heads-up: we have a short maintenance window tonight 03:00 UTC to roll runtime config + service restart on dedicated pools. scope: config flags + model-version pin tweaks for riskier routes. expected impact: 1-3 minute connection drop per pool, rare 502s. need: a 1-line public statuspage, an email for impacted customers, and an ops FAQ for support. who can draft?
deploy-bot: schedule=2026-06-20T03:00:00Z; canary=15m; stage-rollout=90m; rollback-on-error>7pct_for_5m; notify-channel=#eng-platform; runbook=/runbooks/runtime-restart-2026-06-20.md
nina_support: I'll take the customer copy and short status blurb. Posting drafts here for review.
nina_support: STATUSPAGE (public): "Routine maintenance: rolling runtime update for dedicated inference pools in select regions. You may see brief request errors (up to ~3 minutes per pool) during restarts. No customer data will be affected. Window: 03:0000Z04:00Z."
nina_support: EMAIL (impacted customers): "Subject: Notice: Redwood runtime update (03:00 UTC)

Hello —

We're performing a routine runtime and pool restart tonight at 03:00 UTC to deploy stability and performance fixes. Impact: during the restart of each pool you may observe short request errors (typically 13 minutes) or slightly increased latency. We will: 
- Pin your workload to the active runtime snapshot for the duration if you are on our critical SLA list.
- Monitor metrics and auto-rollback if error rates exceed thresholds.
- Send an update once the rollout completes or if we pause/rollback.

No action is required unless this time conflicts with a strict production window. To request a manual pin or coordinate a different window, reply to this email or contact support@redwood.com.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Operations"

infra_lee: tiny wording request: in the statuspage line let's avoid exact minutes; say "short interruptions" instead of "up to 3 minutes". Keeps expectations broad.
chris: good point. nina, change the line.
nina_support: updated STATUSPAGE: "Routine maintenance: rolling runtime update for dedicated inference pools in select regions. You may see short interruptions to requests while pools restart. No customer data will be affected. Window: 03:00 UTC 1 04:00 UTC."
sam_ops: adding ops FAQ notes (short):
- What will customers see? Short request failures (502/503) and transient latency.
- Will inference continue? Yes, majority of routing will go to warm pools; some requests may be retried.
- Can we pin customers? Yes; we will pin listed critical customers before the window. See pin command below.
- Notifications: statuspage + email + direct outreach for pinned customers.

sam_ops: PIN COMMAND EXAMPLE (ops-only):
```
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/pins" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"customer_id":"cust-789","route":"/v1/generate","model":"rwd-13b-quant","version":"2026-05-12"}'
```
kate_product: recommend adding a small reassurance around quality checks: "We will hold canary if generation quality or error signals degrade beyond safe thresholds and notify customers." Put that in both email and statuspage details (ops FAQ).
chris: agreed. also: who will publish the statuspage? nina?
nina_support: I will schedule the short statuspage publish at 02:30 UTC (30m before). Email broadcast to impacted list at T+10 once canary starts (03:10 UTC) with live update link.
sam_ops: i'll prepare the pinned-customer list and send to nina by 18:00 UTC today. It will include route identifiers and model version hashes.
chris: post-rollout ask: export token-level cost delta and a quick quality delta report (sample prompts) for product/qa. tag product_qa channel.
nina_support: copy that. I'll include the support contact alias and localized time conversions in the email.
chris: ok final: keep this thread as the single source of truth for messaging edits. if deploy-bot changes schedule it should update the thread automatically. thanks.
